newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher on snow, shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher on snow, shortcovering.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed higher Friday, due largely to shortcovering after declines Thursday, traders said.
One trader theorized buying was motivated by snow in the Texas panhandle plus ideas Thursday's declines were excessive.
"This is a technical bounce after Thursday's sharply lower close," said another trader earlier in the day.

An underlying factor was news Thursday the European Union placed a tax on wheat exports, a move intended to ensure enough wheat for domestic needs. The action also largely removed a major exporter from the global wheat market.

The snow in Texas may cause lodging and hurt some of the wheat damaged in the freeze two weeks ago. But an agronomist said the snow damage should be minimal, plus the moisture could aid development of tillers that survived the freeze.
KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed up two to 10 cents with May up two at $4.70 per bushel and July up eight at $4.53.
KCBT wheat estimated wheat volume was 44.485 million bushels versus 76.890 million Thursday.
